reviews.decision: The whole patch adds the modern chipGrid getter/private _chipGrid backing field and a new chipRemovedChanges removal-request stream, including both public API hunks. The owned legacy input retains its original setter-only chipList/_chipList members, with all29 class members identical to the untouched tagged16 class. Its legacy chipRemoveChanges is a distinct destruction-event stream merging chip.destroyed, not chip.removed despite its comment/name. Both old and candidate source protocols observe only destroy-a/destroy-b after interleaved removal requests/destruction; changing that existing stream would break the historical destruction-driven contract. No current MatChipInput/Grid/Set ownership route exists. Neither a renamed accessor nor a new modern public stream is required to preserve the historical contract; no API is mirrored and no native runtime pass is claimed.

original_analysis.subject: feat(material/chips): make ChipInput optional for MatChipGrid (#31693)

reviews.decision: The complete optional feature adds the public SeparatorKey interface and widens both input/default option types and matching semantics across four full changed paths, including API goldens. The legacy input and owned default-options declarations retain readonly number[] | ReadonlySet<number>; every input class member matches untouched tagged16. Across288 array/set/key/modifier traces per genuine original16.2.14 and advertised-minimum21.2.14/22.1.7 public helper, the candidate matches tagged numeric-only modifier rejection and getter order. The original modern feature separately accepts ctrl plus shift when ctrl is requested because the helper uses a disjunction; no exact-only modifier set is inferred from the test name. This additive modern feature is outside preserving Material16 behavior and would create a modern API mirror; retain the historical contract rather than adding an unrequired type/option surface. No resource or consumer changes, native execution or minimum-floor credit follow from these source protocols.
